html:
Tatau is the Samoan art of tattooing, done with bone combs tapped into the skin. The man's peʻa covers him from waist to knees; the woman's malu marks the thighs. The English word tattoo comes from the Polynesian tatau.

It is an old art shared across Polynesia. Missionaries in the 19th century tried to stamp it out, and in many islands it died, but Samoa kept it alive through a few families of master tattooists.

Receiving the peʻa is a test of courage and a mark of service to family and village. Since the 1970s it has spread to the Samoan diaspora and helped revive tattooing in Tonga, Tahiti and among the Māori.
